findings: 28-utility-reconnection-fee-explained.md: Added disconnection triggers by utility type (electric, gas, water, seasonal/moratorium), an 8-row typical-fee table with state/utility examples citing PG&E Rule 23, Con Edison tariff leaf 140, PECO Rule 14, PSE&G sheet 63, Consumers Energy, Georgia Power, CPS Energy. 23-utility-billing-cycle-explained.md: Added why cycle lengths vary (meter-read schedules, weekend/holiday shifts, seasonal routing, cycle-day grouping). Added long-vs-short-month bill math with worked January/February example table (28 vs 33 days, identical daily usage). Added estimated-vs-actual read interaction table with 'How Estimated Reads Affect Your Bill' explanation. Added 'How to Check Your Cycle Dates' table. Cited EIA average 899 kWh/month baseline.

how-sewer-charges-work-on-your-water-bill.md: Added three sewer billing models (metered water-based, flat fee, ERU) each with worked calculations. Added winter averaging section with December–March worked example (4-month average = 7.75 CCF). Added three real utility examples: Seattle Public Utilities ($8.44/CCF winter-averaged), Philadelphia Water ($10.22/CCF tier 1), San Francisco PUC ($6.48/CCF tiered). All cited to utility rate pages.

44-how-to-lower-water-bill.md: Complete transformation from investigation content to genuine action page. Ranked actions by cost level (Level 1 free behaviors, Level 2 leak repairs, Level 3 fixture upgrades, Level 4 outdoor/irrigation, Level 5 full-load disciplines). Every savings range cited from EPA WaterSense 'Start Saving' page. Added payback table ranked by fastest return. Added GoveeLife Water Leak Detector 1s 5-pack+gateway (B0DQLFC3Q6) with disclosure in 'Catch Silent Leaks' section. Links to 06-water-bill-too-high and CCF calculator at top for diagnose-first readers.
All 4 pages exceed 800 body words (1652, 1355, 1518, 1728 respectively). All frontmatter updated to 2026-08-28. All factual claims sourced from EPA, DOE, EIA, CFPB, or HHS.
